transcript.text: I'd like to share an important finding from my classroom trial. I conducted a trial this week with the enrolled section, and the results showed that all 12 students need simultaneous stations — each student requires one laptop and one USB microphone. I recorded these results in my classroom planning log, but I should note that the log was not attached to the capital request. Based on this trial, the request for 10 laptops may be insufficient; we likely need 12 laptops and 12 USB microphones to serve all enrolled students properly.

transcript.text: Thank you, Dr. Monroe. I'd like to share the findings from my network and privacy review. I completed the technology review ticket this week, and the key finding is that the commercial cloud music platform requested in the proposal cannot be used with student accounts due to our network and privacy requirements. Instead, the district-managed SoundLab EDU platform is approved for use. It requires managed student accounts plus a security configuration record. I should note that while I closed the technology review ticket this week, it has not yet been linked to the purchasing request.

transcript.text: Thank you, Dr. Monroe. I'd like to share an important finding from the business office. I received the Arts Innovation Grant award notice this week and filed it in the business-office grant folder, though it hasn't yet been added to the proposal. The key finding is that the Arts Innovation Grant will fund this project, but only up to exactly $6,800 — not the $8,000 requested from the general fund. Additionally, the grant requires that the purchase order be issued by August 20, 2026. Under the grant's purchasing sequence, the purchase order must be followed by procurement and setup, which means September 15, 2026 is the earliest feasible installation date — not the September 1, 2026 date in the draft proposal. So the funding source, funding amount, and installation date all need to be revised based on this grant award.
